title: Case-management software for small independent funeral homes
subtitle: Idea stress-test, quick depth. Customer voice was thin because Capterra, G2 and Reddit were blocked; this verdict rests on what could be read and checked.

verdict.summary: The market is crowded and cheap. About 30 products are listed, with tiers from $49 to $79 a month, a free version and month-to-month terms. Most of the director reviews this run could read praise their current tool. The one sharp complaint, a freezing mobile app, came from a single reviewer, and Gather already sells phone case access. Capterra, G2 and Reddit returned 403, so price and switching complaints there went unread. A cheap check is 10 calls with directors before writing any code.

opportunities.name: Case management for small independent funeral homes
opportunities.one_liner: Cloud case file, arrangements and contracts for 1-3 director homes.
opportunities.why: Pain 4: the friction is real but mild, from 8 reviewers across 6 URLs, and only one wants to leave (e3). Most reviews read were positive (e12-e16). Willingness to pay 6: homes already pay $49 to $469 a month (o7, o8, o9, o12), but no verified price complaint turned up. Competition gap 2: about 30 vendors, cheap and no-contract (o2, o7, o12), and well-liked support (e12, e15, e16). Founder fit 5: Django suits CRUD case files, but state forms (e10) and 15 hours a week to support a 24/7 business are a stretch. Reachability 4: no free public venue where directors complain was found; Reddit was blocked. Build cost 5: months of work at 15 hours a week, plus migrating data out of incumbents.

gap.statement: Small independent funeral directors who work cases from their phone can't get reliable mobile case access because the app they use freezes and logs them out. Evidence is thin: one Passare app review and one TerraPro review.

pains.theme: Mobile and cloud case access is flaky
pains.summary: Apps freeze, log users out and lose notes. One director wants the company to drop the tool.
Old design, too many dialog boxes, a learning curve. One reviewer says a spreadsheet would do.
National products carry sections a state doesn't use. Only one URL, so unverified.
One reviewer notes it and shrugs, since Stripe and QuickBooks cover it. Only one URL, so unverified.

competitors.name: Osiris
competitors.pricing: From $79/mo by call volume on its own pricing page; $65/mo on its SourceForge listing; month-to-month
competitors.positioning: Osiris Software offers worry-free, monthly subscription-based pricing plans.
weaknesses: Capterra complaints could not be read (403)

competitors.name: Gather
competitors.pricing: Not public: activation fee plus monthly
competitors.positioning: Manage any case from your phone, improve collection rates, provide a better family experience, create contracts and collect e-signatures, and enjoy unlimited support, cases, and users.

competitors.name: Passare
strengths: Widely adopted (per search results; not verified)
weaknesses: Mobile app freezes and logs users out

critic.risk: Crowded with cheap, well-liked tools: $49 plus a free version, $65 to $79 with no contract, and praised personal support.
The one sharp pain, mobile access, is already marketed by Gather and is a single release for Passare to fix.
Consolidation: search results say Batesville bought Halcyon and Directors Investment Group owns Passare. Both page fetches returned no text, so this is unverified.
Forms differ by state, and death-care records need trust that a solo side project lacks.
Capterra, G2 and Reddit were blocked, so price and switching complaints there went unread. They could change the pain score.

validation.experiment: Before writing code, call 10 owners of independent homes (1 to 3 directors, found through state funeral director association member lists). Ask what made them switch software last time, what they pay, and whether mobile case access fails them.
validation.pass_bar: 6 of 10 name the same unsolved problem and say they would switch for it at $79 to $149 a month
steps: Day 1-2: pull 30 independent homes from one state association directory
Day 3-6: call or visit, aiming for 10 conversations
Day 7: tally; kill if there is no shared problem

kill_criteria: Fewer than 6 of 10 directors share one unsolved problem
Most are happy with a sub-$100/mo tool
